column1: # gate-buckets.tsv — the yield bucket of every refusal site scripts/check-gate-buckets.sh
# enumerates in the lean lane (#636, item 2 of the #605 epic).
#         `path::name` enforcer key, adopted unchanged. The pair must be one CORPUS declares.
#           gates-llm      a fabrication or self-approval defense. NEVER yields: an attended
#                          session cannot approve its own work any more than an unattended one
#                          can, because what is missing is independence, not attendance.
#           gates-signal   the fact is objective — a lane is red, a hash moved, a file is frozen.
#                          NEVER yields either, and this bucket exists so that "no gate is
#                          unclassified" is satisfiable without making a red suite waivable.
#           gates-process  the premise is "no human is available to answer this". MAY yield.
#           not-a-gate     NOT a bucket. The shape enumerator over-enumerates — environment
#                          refusals, usage errors and exit-0 success paths all match it — and this
#                          is the value that gives them a home so the enum can close. A row here
#                          must OPEN its `why` with which of the three it is, and that is checked.
# anchor  A distinctive substring of the site's LINE. Text, never a line number: a `file:line`
#         key would red on every unrelated edit above it, and a guard that cries wolf gets
#         baselined away. The anchor must still appear in the file (absence is ANCHOR DRIFT = red)
#         and must still cover at least one live enumerated site (a row that outlived its site is
#         also red). An anchor MAY cover several sites; the guard prints the count per row so a
#         loose one is visible rather than silent.
# yield   `-` for every bucket but `gates-process`. For `gates-process`, either an
#         OVERRIDE_GATES / OVERRIDE_SCOPES value — read from operator-override.sh at run time, not
#         copied — or `unwired — <reason>`. THE SAFETY ARM IS THIS COLUMN, not code proximity: a
#         row whose yield cell names an override value MUST be gates-process, which is what stops
#         a future edit from wiring a red test lane to an operator waiver.
# why     What makes this disposition true. Not "looks fine" — name the mechanism.
# THE COUNT IS NOT THE CONTRACT. `check-gate-buckets.sh --list` prints the denominator, and this
# file must cover it exactly. That pair is the contract, and neither half can rot without the
# GRANULARITY. One row per enumerated site is the default. Two places take the sanctioned
# exception of one anchor over several sites, and both are visible in the printed counts:
#   * the `envfail` classes (OR-1's recorded default) — 132 sites, 6 rows. The exit-2 contract is
#     what makes every one of them `not-a-gate`, so per-site rows would add no classification.
#   * `orchestrate-lean.sh`'s `terminal <slug> <code>` sites, keyed on the slug. Two calls with
#     the same slug are the same decision point reached from two call paths (the resume path and
#     the fresh path); dispositioning them apart would be a distinction with no referent.
# MOST gates-process ROWS ARE LEGITIMATELY `unwired`, and OR-2 settles that they may stay so:
# only two OVERRIDE_GATES values exist today and both are intake-side. The guard checks the FORM
# of the cell, never the existence of a follow-up ticket.
